title: How Does a Squirrel Find 3,000 Buried Nuts? 🐿️
description:
A squirrel can bury around 3,000 nuts in one season, and it finds most of them again using a memory map of landmarks plus its sense of smell. The nuts it never digs up are already planted, which is how squirrels help new trees grow.

topic: Why do squirrels bury nuts they never dig up?
script: Your backyard squirrel buries 3,000 nuts a year. How does it find them? Each one goes in its own little hole. Mostly, it remembers. It builds a map in its head, a tree, a rock, a fence post, and that map can last up to two months. Then its nose finds the exact spot. But what if another squirrel is watching? It fakes it. It digs a hole, pretends to drop the nut, and sneaks off with it still in its mouth. Sneaky, right? Still, some nuts never get dug up. The squirrel moves on, or it just has plenty to eat. And that forgotten nut is already planted. Come spring, it sprouts. So some trees around you were planted by a squirrel that forgot. Which tree near you did a squirrel plant?
key_facts: A squirrel can bury up to about 3,000 nuts in a single season (PopSci, Reconnect With Nature)
Spatial memory does most of the work; smell helps; memory is strong for weeks and up to about two months (PopSci)
Squirrels sometimes fake-bury a nut while keeping it in their mouth when watched (PopSci)
Forgotten nuts can grow into trees and aid forest regeneration (Reconnect With Nature)
